title: `prompts/list`
description: Lists the prompt templates a server exposes, with their names, titles, descriptions and argument definitions.
question: Can the agent discover the server's prompts?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Prompts are the user-controlled primitive: the slash commands and menu entries a server contributes to the host. A framework that ignores them silently discards a third of what the server publishes, and the omission is invisible because nothing errors.

notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface (agents-core `src/mcp.ts`) has tools and resources methods but no prompts method.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `prompts/list` is unreachable.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no prompts API (no list, get or loader for prompts), so there is no route to `prompts/list`.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpPrompt` holds `name`, `description` and `arguments`; `prompts/list` loses each prompt's `title`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ListPrompts` on.
